headline: Gold Set for Worst Week Since March on Hawkish Fed, AI Selloff
author: Yihui Xie

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:56 PM PST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Gold fell and was heading for the biggest weekly decline since March, as a hawkish Federal Reserve signaled more interest-rate cuts and a selloff in AI stocks pushed investors to sell the metal to cover losses.

Bullion dropped as much as 1% on Friday to near $3,590 an ounce, on track to lose more than 7% in a week that's seen the metal slide to the lowest since September 2025. Silver has lost around 13% in the same period. Fed Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee on Thursday joined a number of central bank officials who have hinted at interest-rate hikes, saying he would consider all options to counter stubborn US inflation.

The prospect of tighter monetary policy kept Treasury yields elevated, with 10-year borrowing costs poised to match a 2007 run of 29 closes above 5% in the same year. Higher rates and yields are typically negative for gold, which doesn't pay interest. A gauge of the dollar has also risen 0.7% this week, making bullion priced in the US currency more expensive for most buyers.

Gold has fallen by nearly a third since the US-Iran war began in late February, as higher energy costs fueled inflation. The precious metal has also been caught up in a rout in technology stocks, with Asian equities set to track a decline on Wall Street after Anthropic PBC's solid market debut failed to reverse wider pessimism for the artificial intelligence trade.
Spot gold fell 0.6% to $3,603.40 an ounce at 7:44 a.m. in Singapore. Silver dropped 1% to $42.52 an ounce, after sinking nearly 5% in the previous session. Platinum and palladium also declined.
